events.title: Roald Amundsen Reaches the South Pole
events.description: Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen and his four-man team became the first people to reach the geographic South Pole, arriving ahead of Robert Falcon Scott's British expedition using sled dogs and skis.
events.significance: Marked the achievement of one of the last great goals of terrestrial exploration and showcased the effectiveness of careful planning and polar travel techniques.

events.title: Death of George Washington
events.description: George Washington, first President of the United States and commander of the Continental Army, died at Mount Vernon at age 67 after a sudden illness involving a severe throat infection.
events.significance: His death prompted national mourning; he was eulogized as 'first in war, first in peace, and first in the hearts of his countrymen,' and his precedent of peaceful transfer of power shaped American democracy.

events.title: Alabama Admitted as the 22nd U.S. State
events.description: Alabama was admitted to the Union as the 22nd state, following the cession of Creek lands and rapid settlement of the region driven by cotton cultivation.
events.significance: Alabama's admission reflected the westward expansion of the United States and the growth of the cotton economy, which was closely tied to the expansion of slavery in the South.

events.title: Mariner 2 Flies by Venus
events.description: NASA's Mariner 2 spacecraft passed within about 35,000 km of Venus, becoming the first spacecraft to successfully conduct a close planetary encounter and return scientific data.
events.significance: It revealed Venus's extremely hot surface temperatures and confirmed the solar wind, laying the groundwork for future interplanetary exploration.

events.title: Eugene Cernan Leaves the Moon on Apollo 17
events.description: Astronaut Eugene Cernan, commander of Apollo 17, climbed into the lunar module after the final moonwalk of the Apollo program, becoming the last person to walk on the Moon.
events.significance: Marked the end of crewed lunar exploration of the Apollo era; no human has walked on the Moon since.
